core/schema_shape.py:R5:_collect_sqlite_: isinstance(bind, Connection) discriminates SQLAlchemy's own Inspector.bind union (Engine | Connection | None) so the sqlite_master AUTOINCREMENT probe either reuses the caller's live Connection or opens one from the Engine. Connection is a concrete vendor class, never a runtime_checkable Protocol, so ADR-032 s1 nominal discrimination applies and an impostor cannot walk through it. The value is Tier-1: the bind is constructed by ELSPETH's own probe entry point (core/landscape/database.py:probe_schema_shape, web/sessions/schema.py), not parsed from external input. What it protects is transaction scope, not privilege — taking the Engine branch on a live Connection would open a second connection outside the caller's transaction and read a schema the caller has not committed. Removing the check would require threading a Connection through collect_metadata_shape_issues and its eight helpers, a public-signature and transaction-scoping change to a 2497-line module that is not on this finding's justified axis.
core/schema_shape.py:R5:_proven_pg_catal: isinstance(bind, Connection) discriminates the same SQLAlchemy Inspector.bind union (Engine | Connection | None) for the pg_catalog identity proof. Connection is a concrete vendor class, not a Protocol. Tier-1 value: the bind originates in ELSPETH's own schema-probe entry points. The discrimination protects transaction scope — the proof query runs inside a savepoint on a caller-owned Connection (see _text_builtin_identity_rows_on_connection) and must not silently open a second connection when one is already in a transaction. The else arm of this same chain returns _EMPTY_TEXT_BUILTIN_PROOF, so an unrecognised bind degrades to the strictest proof (fewer recognised equivalences, more reported issues) rather than to a permissive one.

isinstance(bind, Engine) is the second arm of the Inspector.bind union discrimination above, and it is what makes the union exhaustive with an explicit fail-closed else. Engine is a concrete vendor class, not a Protocol; the value is Tier-1 (ELSPETH-constructed bind). Collapsing the two arms into a single duck-typed .connect() call is exactly the structural typing ADR-032 forbids as a discriminator, and would make an unrecognised bind raise AttributeError instead of degrading to _EMPTY_TEXT_BUILTIN_PROOF. The arm protects the fail-closed default: without it, no branch returns the empty proof and a non-Engine non-Connection bind would leave proof_rows unbound.
core/schema_shape.py:R5:_expected_index_: isinstance(expression, Column) discriminates SQLAlchemy's Index.expressions union (Column | ColumnElement | str) to decide whether an index component is a plain column reference or a compiled expression. Column is a concrete vendor class, not a Protocol. The value is Tier-1 — these are ELSPETH's own declared Index objects from web/sessions/models.py, not reflected data — but the union is SQLAlchemy's, not ours, and SQLAlchemy normalises author input into it, so the shape is not knowable by construction at this site. What the check protects is comparison fidelity: a Column recorded as a compiled expression (or the reverse) would make a matching declared/reflected pair compare unequal and raise a spurious schema-shape issue on every startup probe. The conjoined `expression.name in table.c` is a value assertion on top of the type discrimination, so an unattached Column still takes the expression branch.

isinstance(expression, str) separates the pre-compiled-text member of SQLAlchemy's Index.expressions union from a ColumnElement that still needs .compile(). str is a concrete builtin, not a Protocol. The value is Tier-1 (ELSPETH's declared Index metadata) but the union membership is chosen by SQLAlchemy's own normalisation, not by our call site. What it protects is a crash, not a privilege: calling .compile(dialect=..., compile_kwargs=...) on a str raises AttributeError and would abort the whole schema probe, while feeding an uncompiled ColumnElement to _expected_expression_ast would parse its repr as SQL. Neither branch is reachable by construction, so the discrimination cannot be dropped.
core/schema_shape.py:R5:_index_expected_: isinstance(where, str) discriminates the same SQLAlchemy str-or-ColumnElement union for a partial-index predicate read out of index.dialect_options[dialect.name]['where']. str is a concrete builtin, not a Protocol. Tier-1 value (our own declared postgresql_where), vendor-owned union. It protects the compile step: SQLAlchemy accepts either form for `where`, and .compile() on a str raises AttributeError. The comparator is fail-closed downstream — whatever this returns is compared against the reflected predicate and any difference becomes a reported SchemaShapeIssue — so the check exists to reach the comparison at all, not to admit anything.
core/schema_shape.py:R5:_normalize_postg: not isinstance(value, Mapping) is a genuine Tier-3 shape guard: one of this helper's two callers is _actual_postgresql_operator_classes, which reads reflected['dialect_options']['postgresql_ops'] straight out of a live PostgreSQL reflection, whose shape ELSPETH does not own or pin across server and driver versions. Mapping is a concrete collections.abc ABC, not a runtime_checkable Protocol. Crucially the guard does not silently drop the value: the non-Mapping branch returns (('<invalid>', repr(value))), which flows into the _IndexShape comparison and surfaces as a reported SchemaShapeIssue, so malformed reflection becomes a visible schema difference rather than a silent pass. @trust_boundary is deliberately NOT used here: the other caller, _expected_postgresql_operator_classes, passes Tier-1 declared Index(postgresql_ops=...) metadata, so decorating the function would assert a Tier-3 boundary that is false for half its callers — precisely the whole-function exemption cloak trust_boundary_suppress.py rules out.
core/schema_shape.py:R5:_ddl_object_appl: isinstance(target, str) reads DDLIf.dialect, a SQLAlchemy-PRIVATE field (obj._ddl_if) whose runtime contract is wider than its `str | None` annotation — the widening is deliberate and documented in the comment two lines above, not an accident to be narrowed away. str is a concrete builtin, not a Protocol. The value is Tier-1 (ELSPETH authors every .ddl_if(dialect=...) call, all in web/sessions/models.py) but the annotation cannot be trusted as the invariant because the vendor's own runtime accepts more than it declares. A mis-discrimination here grants no privilege: it only mis-scopes which dialect a constraint applies to, and the comparator is fail-closed — a wrongly-scoped constraint shows up as a reported SchemaShapeIssue. Swapping to `type(target) is str` would shed the finding while changing the semantics only for str subclasses, i.e. borrowing an idiom for its lint signature rather than its meaning.

isinstance(target, (tuple, list, set)) is the sequence half of the same documented widening over SQLAlchemy's private DDLIf.dialect field, whose runtime accepts these forms despite the narrower `str | None` annotation. tuple, list and set are concrete builtins, not Protocols. Tier-1 value with a vendor-owned runtime contract. Deleting this arm to shed the finding would be a silent behavioural narrowing: a multi-dialect ddl_if would then fall through `target != dialect.name` and be treated as applying to no dialect at all, reporting spurious differences. It protects comparison fidelity only — no privilege decision depends on it.

isinstance(obj, Index) dispatches this function's own declared union parameter (obj: Constraint | Index) onto the matching SQLAlchemy DDL element, CreateIndex or CreateConstraint, so the ddl_if callable receives the element type it expects. This is ADR-032 s1 in its plain form: nominal discrimination of an internal union against a concrete class, never a Protocol. The value is Tier-1 — the object is one of ELSPETH's own declared Index/Constraint metadata objects. isinstance rather than exact-type identity is deliberate: Constraint has many concrete subclasses (CheckConstraint, UniqueConstraint, ForeignKeyConstraint) and subclass-inclusive dispatch is the intent.
core/schema_shape.py:R5:_undouble_percen: not isinstance(value, tuple) is the leaf test of a recursion over _Ast, this module's OWN type alias (tuple[Any, ...]) built by its own SQL expression parser: a node is a tuple, anything else is a scalar leaf (str, int, None) that is returned unchanged. tuple is a concrete builtin, not a Protocol, and the recursion's parameter is typed `object` precisely because it walks both nodes and leaves. The value is Tier-1: every _Ast reaching here was constructed by _expression_ast / _expected_expression_ast in this module. What it protects is termination and correctness of the '%%' -> '%' undoubling, which must reach literals at any depth without iterating into a str character-by-character. There is no owned node class to discriminate against — _Ast is a structural tuple alias by design, matching how the comparator hashes and compares shapes.
core/audit_export_content_store.py:R7:_e: suppress(FileExistsError) around os.mkdir(part, mode=0o700, dir_fd=current) is not error swallowing: FileExistsError IS the success case of an idempotent, race-hardened directory walk — it means another process created this component first. The suppression is exactly one concrete exception type; PermissionError, NotADirectoryError and every other OSError still propagate. The postcondition is re-established and PROVEN by the very next statement, os.open(part, O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, dir_fd=current), which raises if the name is not a directory or is a symlink, and by the trailing stat check that rejects any root whose mode has group or other bits. Replacing it with a pre-existence check would open the TOCTOU window this content store is specifically hardened against (the O_NOFOLLOW/dir_fd walk exists for that reason); replacing it with try/except FileExistsError: pass would trade R7 for R6 with strictly less clarity. The value is Tier-2 operator-supplied export path, and what this protects is the audit-export content store's private-directory invariant.

suppress(FileExistsError) around os.mkdir(name, mode=0o700, dir_fd=parent_fd) is the same race-free create-or-reuse step, scoped to one namespace component under an already-opened parent descriptor. FileExistsError is the concurrent-creation success case, not a failure; every other OSError (PermissionError, NotADirectoryError, ENOSPC) still propagates. The function's return statement — os.open(name, O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, dir_fd=parent_fd) — re-establishes and proves the postcondition and raises if the name is not a directory or is a symlink, so the suppression cannot hide a missing or hostile path from the caller. A stat-then-mkdir form would be a TOCTOU regression in a store that deliberately never resolves a path by name after opening its parent.
core/llm_profiles.py:L1:_module_:ast=imp: This lazy L1->L3 import is retained after walking ADR-006's Violation #11 Protocol and finding every removal option blocked at this site. (1) 'Move the needed code down': _validate_provider_binding needs the provider config CLASSES, not just their names — it does a membership check AND constructs providers['bedrock'](...) / providers['gateway'](...) to reuse their field validators. Those models live in plugins/transforms/llm/providers/*.py fused with their runtime clients; gateway.py alone imports httpx, structlog, AuditedHTTPClient and plugin telemetry, so the module cannot move to core. (2) 'Extract the primitive portion and move that down' would mean splitting config models from clients across four provider modules — a real architectural change well beyond a justify burn-down, and one that would rewrite the highest-churn LLM code. (3) 'Restructure the caller so it does not need the cross-layer code' means reimplementing the provider allowlist in core, which recreates the divergent SECOND provider allowlist that this validator exists to prevent (see the module docstring and LLM_PROFILE_PRIVATE_FIELDS: web and batch must lower the same alias to identical bindings). The import is function-local, so elspeth.core remains importable without elspeth.plugins and no module-scope coupling exists; the runtime coupling is one registry read at profile-validation time. This is residual architectural debt with a known shape, not a convenience import — it is surfaced on the bucket issue for a follow-up that splits the provider config models from their clients. The sibling L1 in this module (elspeth.plugins.infrastructure.url_validation) was REMOVED in this lane by ADR-006 Phase 1's own remedy: the module was stdlib-only, so it moved to core/url_validation.py and this import became a top-level core->core one.
core/commencement_gate_expression.py:R5:: isinstance(node, ast.Constant) discriminates a stdlib CPython AST node type inside an ast.NodeTransformer. ast.Constant is a concrete class produced only by CPython's own parser — it is not a runtime_checkable Protocol and cannot be duck-typed past, and _visit_lookup_key's parameter is typed ast.expr (the whole expression union), so the concrete node kind is genuinely unknown at this site. The value's provenance is Tier-2 operator-authored gate condition text, already parsed by ExpressionParser against COMMENCEMENT_GATE_ALLOWED_NAMES before ast.parse runs here. What the check protects is elspeth-83261b699c, the leak this redactor exists to close: a direct string subscript key is structural and is RETAINED for diagnosis, while every other expression falls through to self.visit and has its string literals replaced with <redacted-string-literal>. Structural discrimination on a grammar node is the redactor's whole job; there is no owned type to discriminate against because the tree belongs to the stdlib parser.

isinstance(node.value, str) narrows an already-identified ast.Constant to the string case, because ast.Constant also carries ints, floats, bools, None, bytes and Ellipsis and only string constants can carry secret material into audit or error text. str is a concrete builtin, not a Protocol. Tier-2 operator-authored condition text. This conjunct is the one that keeps the retain branch narrow: without it a non-str constant key would also be retained on the assumption it was a lookup key, and the pair (Constant AND str) is what makes the redaction rule 'retain a direct string map key, redact everything else' exact. Failing this test costs nothing — the node falls through to self.visit and is redacted, the safe direction.

isinstance(node.value, str) is the redactor's core decision: NodeTransformer dispatch guarantees the node is an ast.Constant, but ast.Constant.value is a union of every literal type CPython admits, and only str values can echo a secret into a commencement-gate audit or error message (elspeth-83261b699c). str is a concrete builtin, not a Protocol. Tier-2 operator-authored condition text. The check is what makes this method a redactor rather than a no-op, and it fails safe in the only direction that matters — a str value is always replaced with <redacted-string-literal>, and numeric/bool/None constants are structural and returned as-is so the unparsed shape stays diagnosable.

isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute) discriminates a stdlib AST node kind to recognise the `<name>.get(key)` map-lookup form the restricted commencement-gate grammar admits. ast.Attribute is a concrete CPython parser class, not a Protocol; ast.Call.func is typed as the full ast.expr union, so the kind is genuinely unknown here. Tier-2 operator-authored condition text, pre-validated by ExpressionParser. It protects the redaction boundary in the safe direction: only a call that satisfies ALL FOUR conjuncts (Attribute func, Name receiver, receiver in COMMENCEMENT_GATE_ALLOWED_NAMES, attr == 'get') keeps its argument as a structural lookup key; every other call falls through to generic_visit and has its string arguments redacted. A mis-discrimination therefore over-redacts, never under-redacts.

isinstance(node.func.value, ast.Name) is the receiver half of the same four-conjunct map-lookup recognition, and it is the conjunct that makes the following COMMENCEMENT_GATE_ALLOWED_NAMES membership test possible at all: only an ast.Name has an .id to compare against the closed allowed-names tuple ('collections', 'dependency_runs'). ast.Name is a concrete CPython parser class, not a Protocol. Tier-2 operator-authored condition text. What it protects is the allowlist itself — without the Name discrimination an arbitrary attribute chain ending in .get(...) would reach the key-retaining branch and could carry a literal through unredacted. It fails toward redaction, which is the safe direction for this gate.
